## Tuning Parameters

```{r}
#| label: ocf-param-info
#| echo: false
defaults <-
  tibble::tibble(
    parsnip = c(
      "mtry", "trees", "min_n", "max.depth",
      "sample.fraction", "honesty", "honesty.fraction",
      "replace", "alpha"
    ),
    default = c(
      "see below", "500L", "5L", "0L",
      "see below", "FALSE", "0.5",
      "FALSE", "0.2"
    )
  )

param <-
  rand_forest() |>
  set_engine("ocf") |>
  make_parameter_list(defaults)
```

This model has `r nrow(param)` tuning parameters:

```{r ocf-param-list, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
param$item
```

`mtry` depends on the number of columns and the model mode. The default in [ocf::ocf()] is `ceiling(sqrt(ncol(x)))`.

`sample.fraction` defaults to `1` when `replace = TRUE` and to `0.5` otherwise.

`alpha` is the minimum fraction of parent observations in each split; it is restricted to `[0, 0.5]`.

`max.depth = 0` allows unlimited depth; the `tree_depth()` dial covers only positive finite depths.

## Translation from parsnip to the original package (classification)

```{r, ocf-cls}
library(ordered)

rand_forest(
  mtry = integer(1),
  trees = integer(1),
  min_n = integer(1)
) |>
  set_engine(
    "ocf",
    sample.fraction = 0.5,
    honesty = FALSE,
    replace = FALSE,
    alpha = 0.2,
    max.depth = 0
  ) |>
  set_mode("classification") |>
  translate()
```

## Preprocessing requirements

Factor predictors are converted to full sets of indicator variables (one-hot encoding). No intercept is included.

## Other notes

By default, parallel processing is turned off. To change it, use the `n.threads` argument via [set_engine()].

## Prediction types

```{r}
#| label: predict-types

  dplyr::filter(engine == "ocf") |>
  dplyr::select(mode, type)
```
